chapters.category: Ethiopic textual tradition • Modern English research translation
chapters.title: Chapter 70 — Enoch Is Raised to the Place of the Righteous
chapters.sourceNote: Translated afresh into clear modern English from the earliest complete primary-language text responsibly available for this chapter. No extant Aramaic or Greek wording has been identified for this concluding unit of the Parables. The complete Ethiopic (Geʽez) text in August Dillmann's 1851 critical edition, Liber Henoch Aethiopice, is the translation base for all four verses: the raising of Enoch's living name to the Son of Man and the Lord of Spirits, his ascent on spiritual chariots, his placement between the two winds, and his vision of the ancient fathers and righteous. The compact shifts in person found in the source are retained as closely as clear English permits. No unattested wording was supplied, and no modern English translation was used as the translation base.

verses.text: After this, his living name was raised to that Son of Man and to the Lord of Spirits, away from those who dwell on the dry ground.
verses.study: Enoch's identity is transferred from the earthly community into the presence of the Son of Man and the Lord of Spirits. The raising of his living name presents divine recognition as more enduring than earthly location.
crossReferences: Genesis 5:24 — Enoch is taken by God
Daniel 7:13–14 — the Son of Man stands in the heavenly presence

verses.text: He was raised on the chariots of the spirit, and his name went out from among them.
verses.study: The spiritual chariots mark a heavenly conveyance rather than an achievement by human strength. Enoch's removal from among earth dwellers is decisive.
crossReferences: 2 Kings 2:11 — Elijah is taken up with a heavenly chariot
Ezekiel 1:19–21 — the living chariot moves by the spirit

verses.text: From that day I was no longer counted among them. He placed me between the two winds, between north and west, where the angels took cords to measure for me a place for the chosen and the righteous.
verses.study: The first-person voice locates Enoch outside his former earthly numbering and within a measured heavenly inheritance. The cords signify an allotted place prepared in ordered space for the righteous.
crossReferences: Zechariah 2:1–2 — a measuring cord marks an appointed holy place
Revelation 21:15–17 — the angel measures the prepared city and its boundaries

verses.text: There I saw the ancient fathers and the righteous, who have dwelt in that place from the beginning of the age.
verses.study: Enoch's destination is a community, not solitary escape. The ancient righteous already dwelling there connect his reception with the enduring hope of those who have remained faithful.
crossReferences: Hebrews 11:13–16 — the faithful ancestors seek a heavenly homeland
Hebrews 12:22–23 — the righteous are gathered in the heavenly assembly

explanation.heading: Chapter teaching and context
paragraphs: Chapter 70 completes the Parables by moving Enoch from earthly testimony into the heavenly presence he has described. His living name is raised to the Son of Man and the Lord of Spirits.
The ascent is attributed to spiritual chariots, emphasizing divine initiative. Enoch does not climb into heaven by secret mastery; he is carried and placed there.
The measured place between the winds expresses preparation and order. The chosen and righteous have an allotted home whose boundaries are established by heavenly authority.
Enoch finds the ancient fathers and righteous already dwelling there. The conclusion therefore joins personal translation with the wider hope of a faithful community gathered before God.

crossReferences: Genesis 5:21–24 — Enoch walks with God and is taken
2 Kings 2:11 — heavenly conveyance at Elijah's departure
Daniel 7:13–14 — the Son of Man in the divine court
Hebrews 11:5 — Enoch is translated from death
Hebrews 12:22–23 — the assembly of the righteous in heaven
